messages.author: 275b133a3506805a
messages.subject: NaNs appearing in regression model
parts:
Hi all,

I'm doing a kind of semi-supervised regression. The code and toy data
are at: https://gist.github.com/danstowell/6828740

With this code (in stan 1.3), I'm getting a lot of errors with NaN
values, preventing it from running:

"""
Iteration: 1 / 2000 [ 0%] (Adapting)
alpha: 3.76273:0
sigma: 1e-06:0
tendencies_alpha: [1.73544:0,0.618637:0,0.553649:0,0.529565:0]
tendencies_beta: [0.5:0,0.5:0,0.5:0,0.5:0]

Informational Message: The parameter state is about to be Metropolis
rejected due to the following underlying, non-fatal (really) issue
(and please ignore that what comes next might say 'error'): Error in
function stan::prob::exponential_log(N4stan5agrad3varE): Random
variable is nan:0, but must not be nan!
If the problem persists across multiple draws, you might have a
problem with an initial state or a gradient somewhere.
If the problem does not persist, the resulting samples will still be
drawn from the posterior.
"""
(...this message then repeats a lot, until fail.)

If you comment out the exponential priors, you get a similar message
except that the choking happens in beta_log() instead.

I'm scratching my head about these errors because all my parameters
are fairly narrowly constrained, initialised humanely, and as far as I
can tell there's no log(0)... so I don't see where the nans are coming
from!

Thanks for any thoughts you can offer.

Best
Dan
--
http://www.mcld.co.uk

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] NaNs appearing in regression model
parts:
About the best I can offer is to print as you go and
see where the NaN is coming from. It looks like one
of the left-hand sides of one of these:

alpha ~ exponential(0.5);
sigma ~ exponential(2.0);
tendencies_alpha ~ exponential(0.5);
tendencies_beta ~ exponential(0.5);

And this shouldn't happen in the model you sent because they're
all constrained pretty narrowly.

It looks like sigma is pinned right up against its
declared boundary, which is always a bad sign.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] NaNs appearing in regression model
parts:
My guess is that you have initial values for parameters
that are illegal. This can happen two ways: (a) you
read in illegal initial values, and (b) you have illegal
transformed parameters.

If you take system default inits and there's no transformed
parameters block, then indeed lp__ should print 0 initially.

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] NaNs appearing in regression model
parts:
The problem is that you're sending in values of 1 to
a beta distribution, which returns -infinity. It's support
is only on the open interval (0,1).

You can see it with these prints inside your M_trn loop:

print("proby_trn[",m,"]=",proby_trn[m]);
print("tendencies_alpha=",tendencies_alpha,"; tendencies_beta=",tendencies_beta);
print("beta, m=", m, "; log prob=", beta_log(proby_trn[m], tendencies_alpha, tendencies_beta));

So it's a problem with data, not with inits.

- Bob

Gosh! Thanks for spotting that. It's actually news to me that the
support is (0,1) not [0,1]. Scanning some online references (no
textbooks with me right now), I see a mixture of the two. Even more
relevant, the Stan manual says "\theta \in [0,1]", both in v1.3 and in
latest git:
<https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/blob/develop/src/docs/stan-reference/distributions.tex#L1448>

Anyway - thanks again, and for illustrating how to dig into it. My
model is now running :)

Thanks
Dan

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] NaNs appearing in regression model
parts:
We should change the doc. We're torn between
trying to support the boundary conditions and trying
to return informative error messages. For 0 and 1,
we return -infinity (unless beta=0 and alpha=0
respectively), whereas for values outside of [0,1]
we throw an exception.

- Bob

On 10/7/13 6:30 AM, Dan Stowell wrote:
> Gosh! Thanks for spotting that. It's actually news to me that the
> support is (0,1) not [0,1]. Scanning some online references (no
> textbooks with me right now), I see a mixture of the two. Even more
> relevant, the Stan manual says "\theta \in [0,1]", both in v1.3 and in
> latest git:
> <https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/blob/develop/src/docs/stan-reference/distributions.tex#L1448>
>
> Anyway - thanks again, and for illustrating how to dig into it. My
> model is now running :)
>
> Thanks
> Dan
>
>
> 2013/10/7 Bob Carpenter <ca...@alias-i.com>:
>> The problem is that you're sending in values of 1 to
>> a beta distribution, which returns -infinity. It's support
>> is only on the open interval (0,1).
>>
>> You can see it with these prints inside your M_trn loop:
>>
>> print("proby_trn[",m,"]=",proby_trn[m]);
>> print("tendencies_alpha=",tendencies_alpha,";
>> tendencies_beta=",tendencies_beta);
>> print("beta, m=", m, "; log prob=", beta_log(proby_trn[m],
>> tendencies_alpha, tendencies_beta));
>>
>> So it's a problem with data, not with inits.
>>
>> - Bob
>>
>>
